statuses.built: Implemented in Plexiform and covered by tests (fake provider fixtures unless a real run is recorded).
statuses.unverified: Plexiform has the adapter code path (shared and fake-tested) but it has never been accepted against this provider; it stays unavailable.
statuses.supported-not-built: A primary provider doc or local --help/schema shows a supported channel; Plexiform does not use it yet.
statuses.provider-only: The provider offers it only to its own apps/accounts; not available to a third-party app like Plexiform.
statuses.unsupported: No supported channel found in primary docs or local --help/schema.
statuses.not-applicable: The concept does not exist for this platform.

platforms.label: Claude Code
platforms.hosting: local CLI; Claude Code on the web / --cloud sessions are Anthropic-hosted
platforms.management: owned: Plexiform-started `claude -p` stream-json child (built); existing terminal/IDE sessions: observe only
platforms.channel: Owned: `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --replay-user-messages` (src/claude-code-session.js). Existing: hooks (hooks/set-status.js) for observation only.

telemetry.how: Hooks: working, waiting on permission, subagents, cost/limits.

taskReporting.how: Board/MCP self-report (native-board) and work capture; task text is self-reported, never read from transcripts.

receive.how: Owned sessions only: our stream-json user line with our uuid; ack = command_lifecycle queued/started for that uuid in our --session-id.

reply.how: Owned: stream_event text_delta + result in our session id.

resume.how: `claude -p --resume <id>` continues a finished session in a NEW process; it is not inbound control of a live terminal session. The board runner (board/runner/backends/claude.js) uses it for managed runs.

steer.how: No expected-turn precondition: a message sent mid-turn is queued as the next turn.

remoteControl.how: Remote Control (`claude --remote-control`) lets claude.ai/code and the Claude apps drive a local session; Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise login, not an API for other apps.

handoff.existingSessions: A Stop hook may return decision:block with a reason that continues the turn (documented); Plexiform does not use it: no delivery ack and it only fires when the turn ends.

platforms.prerequisite: None for owned sessions (Claude Code installed and signed in with its own login). Existing sessions: none possible.
platforms.tos: Plexiform runs the user's own CLI with its own login; it never reads, copies or proxies Claude credentials. Remote Control is Anthropic's own surface and is not used.

reasons.existing: Claude Code terminal sessions have no supported inbound message channel; only sessions Plexiform starts with claude -p stream-json can be driven.

evidence: test: test/owned-adapters.test.js (fake stream-json fixture); real run notes plexiform-codex-claude-notes/session-interaction

platforms.label: Codex
platforms.hosting: local app-server; Codex Cloud tasks are OpenAI-hosted
platforms.management: owned: Plexiform-spawned `codex app-server` stdio threads (built); existing desktop/IDE threads: observe only
platforms.channel: Owned: app-server JSON-RPC thread/start, turn/start, turn/steer, turn/interrupt (src/codex-app-server.js). Existing: hooks (adapters/codex.js).

discovery.how: Codex hooks + lifecycle (adapters/codex.js); app-server thread/list and thread/loaded/list exist but only on the server you connect to.

telemetry.how: Hooks: activity, waiting, completed turns, subagents (observation only).

taskReporting.how: Self-report (src/agent-self-report.js, labelled self-reported) and board capture.

receive.how: Owned threads only: turn/start returns the server turn id; echo = clientUserMessageId in the turn's input.

reply.how: item/agentMessage/delta and turn/completed for our thread.

resume.how: thread/resume reopens a stored thread on the server you started; desktop-app threads live on that app's private app-server.

steer.how: turn/steer with expectedTurnId: Codex itself refuses if it is not the active turn.

remoteControl.how: `codex app-server daemon` + control socket and `codex app-server proxy` (local --help); CLI sessions must be started on the daemon by the human. Codex Cloud: `codex cloud exec|status|list|apply|diff` submit/inspect tasks; no follow-up into an existing cloud task.

platforms.prerequisite: None for owned threads (Codex installed and signed in, its login stays in CODEX_HOME). Existing desktop-app threads: a provider-published socket; the private ~/.codex/ipc socket is refused. CLI sessions: the human must opt to run them on the app-server daemon (not built).
platforms.tos: Uses the user's own Codex install and login via the documented app-server; no ChatGPT/Codex app automation, private sockets or chat scraping.

reasons.existing: Plexiform can message sessions it starts itself. This one was started in Codex, which has no supported way for another app to send to it.

evidence: local: `codex app-server --help` (daemon, proxy, generate-json-schema) and `codex cloud --help` (exec/status/list/apply/diff), codex-cli 0.159.2

platforms.label: Cursor
platforms.hosting: Cursor IDE and CLI local; Cloud Agents on Cursor-hosted VMs (or self-hosted pools)
platforms.management: owned: `agent acp` adapter wired but unavailable (not installed, isolation unverified); existing IDE/CLI chats: observe only
platforms.channel: Existing: ~/.cursor/hooks.json (adapters/cursor.js). Owned: ACP over stdio via the shared ACP client (src/acp-agents.js).

telemetry.how: Same hooks; Plexiform replies allow and never gates.

taskReporting.how: Board capture/self-report via MCP; no transcript reading (transcript_path is ignored).

receive.how: Owned: ACP session/prompt; ack = first content session/update for our session. Code path shared with Gemini and tested on a fake ACP agent; never run against Cursor.

resume.how: ACP session/load is documented; Cloud Agents API POST /v1/agents/{id}/runs sends a follow-up to an existing cloud agent (needs a Cursor API key).

steer.how: ACP has no steer; prompts are sequential.

remoteControl.how: Cloud Agents API (Basic/Bearer API key) for Cursor-hosted agents only; no API into existing IDE chats.

handoff.ack: first content session/update for our session
handoff.existingSessions: A stop hook may return followup_message, which Cursor submits as the next user message (documented); Plexiform does not use it: no delivery ack, between turns only.

platforms.prerequisite: Human: install Cursor CLI (`agent`) and sign in (`agent login` or CURSOR_API_KEY in its own environment), then verify on that install that an owned ACP session can be held to ask/plan mode with no user MCP (.cursor/mcp.json is loaded in ACP mode) before Plexiform enables it. Cloud Agents: a Cursor API key Plexiform would have to hold; not done (Plexiform never stores provider logins).
platforms.tos: Uses only documented CLI/ACP/hooks/Cloud Agents API. No IDE automation or chat scraping.

reasons.owned: unavailable: Cursor CLI is installed but Plexiform has not verified on a real install that it can keep your Cursor MCP servers (.cursor/mcp.json) and agent mode out of an owned ACP session; this stays off until that is checked
reasons.existing: Cursor editor and CLI chats have no supported inbound channel for other apps; Cursor's stop hook can only queue a follow-up when a turn ends and Plexiform does not use it.

evidence: test: test/provider-capabilities.test.js (ACP client on fake agent as cursor)

platforms.label: Hermes Agent
platforms.hosting: local agent; model per the user's Hermes config (here a tailnet vLLM)
platforms.management: owned: `hermes acp` reachable through the shared ACP client but kept unavailable (tools cannot be turned off); existing sessions: observe only if the user's Hermes posts to Plexiform's local signal endpoint
platforms.channel: Owned: ACP over stdio (`hermes acp`). Existing: none (Hermes gateway/peer/kanban are Hermes's own messaging surfaces).

discovery.how: Only via Plexiform's local /signal endpoint or emit.js with source hermes (board presence/work-capture accept 'hermes'); Plexiform installs no Hermes hooks.

telemetry.how: Hermes has shell-script hooks (`hermes hooks`); Plexiform does not install them.

taskReporting.how: Self-reported via the signal endpoint / board MCP only.

receive.how: Owned ACP initialize + session/new succeeded on the real install; the one real prompt was not acknowledged within 120 s (see realRuns.hermes). Not offered: see reasons.owned.

reply.how: ACP agent_message_chunk; no reply observed in the one real call.

steer.how: A prompt while a turn runs is queued for the next turn; a prompt starting `/steer` is injected into the running turn (acp_adapter/server.py). No ack tied to our message; not used.

remoteControl.how: Hermes gateway/peer are Hermes-to-platform bridges, not an API into a running session for other apps.

platforms.prerequisite: Hermes would need an ACP option to restrict the session toolset (today ACP sessions always get the hermes-acp toolset: terminal, process, file write/patch, execute_code, delegate_task, web/browser, memory, skills) or Plexiform would need an isolated Hermes profile with those tools disabled, verified by a human.
platforms.tos: User's own local agent and config; no credentials read. Hermes stores ACP sessions in its own state DB.

reasons.owned: unavailable: Hermes ACP sessions always run Hermes's own tools (terminal, file writes, code execution, web, delegate) with your Hermes config and memory, and ACP gives Plexiform no way to switch them off, so Plexiform does not start one
reasons.existing: Hermes sessions started outside Plexiform have no supported inbound channel for other apps.

handoff.existingSessions: Possible via a user-started `opencode serve` (not built).

platforms.tos: Open-source CLI; user's own provider keys stay in OpenCode.

reasons.owned: unavailable: OpenCode is installed but Plexiform has not verified on a real install that an owned ACP session runs with every tool denied; this stays off until that is checked
reasons.existing: OpenCode sessions started outside Plexiform are not connected; OpenCode's own server API would need you to share that server with Plexiform, which is not built.

platforms.label: Claude apps (remote MCP connector)
platforms.hosting: Anthropic-hosted; connector calls come from Anthropic infrastructure to the user's Plexiform hub
platforms.management: neither: the Claude app is a client of Plexiform's remote MCP board tools (docs/remote-mcp.md); Plexiform cannot start or message a Claude chat
platforms.channel: Outgoing only: Streamable HTTP MCP at https://<hub>/api/mcp with OAuth+PKCE grant (read: list/read boards, cards, messages, work context; collaboration: create card, change task text, comment, write packet, send task message).

discovery.how: Plexiform sees only the MCP grant and the tool calls it makes, not chats.

telemetry.how: No lifecycle events from Claude apps.

taskReporting.how: Remote MCP collaboration tools (explicit, grant-scoped, per board).

receive.how: Only the human can prompt the chat; it can pull task messages with the list-messages tool when asked.

reply.how: Pull model: the chat's tool calls (comment/send task message) are its reply; correlation is by card/message reference.

remoteControl.how: Claude's own apps and Remote Control for Claude Code.

handoff.channel: pull only: the chat reads task messages/handovers when its human asks
handoff.ack: tool call receipt (request_id), not chat delivery

platforms.prerequisite: A deployed HTTPS hub with accounts, a custom connector added by the user (or org owner on Team/Enterprise) and a personal board grant; cloud connector acceptance is a separate human gate (docs/remote-mcp.md).
platforms.tos: Uses Anthropic's documented custom-connector path with the user's own consent; no chat scraping.

reasons.owned: unavailable: Claude web and desktop chats cannot be started or messaged by another app; they can only call Plexiform's board tools through a connector you add
reasons.notInstalled: unavailable: Claude web and desktop chats cannot be started or messaged by another app; they can only call Plexiform's board tools through a connector you add
reasons.existing: Claude web and desktop chats have no inbound channel for other apps; they can read task messages through the Plexiform connector when you ask them to.

platforms.label: Custom agent (local signal endpoint)
platforms.hosting: whatever program the user wires up, on this computer
platforms.management: neither: a user's own script, Shortcut or other agent posts activity to Plexiform
platforms.channel: Inbound to Plexiform only: POST 127.0.0.1:47172/signal with the per-install token, or `node hooks/emit.js <signal> --source <name>` (README).

discovery.how: Sessions appear when the program posts signals with a session id.

telemetry.how: Signals: prompt-submit, tool-use, tool-done, tool-failed, stop, permission-ask, limit-hit, idle-nudge, session-start/end, subagent-start/done.

receive.how: The endpoint is one-way; Plexiform has no channel back into an arbitrary program.

platforms.prerequisite: An adapter for that specific program's documented control channel (add a row here first).

reasons.owned: unavailable: Plexiform cannot start a custom agent; it only receives the activity that agent posts
reasons.notInstalled: unavailable: Plexiform cannot start a custom agent; it only receives the activity that agent posts
reasons.existing: This session only reports activity to Plexiform; the program that posts it has no channel for Plexiform to send back.

realRuns.hermes: 2026-10-02, one call, hermes 0.21.3 via src/gemini-acp.js (provider hermes, args ['acp'], verified forced on in a scratch script only) through createInteractionHub in an empty temp cwd: initialize (protocolVersion 1) and session/new OK -> session launched; session/prompt 'Reply with exactly the word PONG' got no content session/update and no prompt response within 120 s -> hub status 'unavailable', delivery 'refused', adapter sent session/cancel, child reaped (no process left). Hermes's configured model is the shared tailnet vLLM, which was saturated at the time (vllm:num_requests_running 4, waiting 1 for capacity). Not retried (one-call budget).
realRuns.localModels: 2026-10-02, one call, src/local-models.js against configured endpoint http://100.68.66.98:8888 (tailnet vLLM, GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3): discovery listed the model (reachable); loopback discovery found nothing on this Mac (11434/1234/8000/8888 closed; :4000 is a non-model 'amass' listener). send -> 'acknowledged' in 23 ms (HTTP 200 stream) but no bytes for 60 s -> turn 'failed: The model stopped responding' (idleMs 60 s). Same saturated backend (4 running, 1 waiting). Send/ack path proven real; a streamed reply on a real endpoint is still unproven.
